title: Environment-Based Endurance Testing in Autonomous Vehicles
summary: Researchers report simulated energy-efficiency gains of about 9.2% from driving advice. The system has not been deployed, so real vehicle and emissions benefits remain unknown.
source_collection: ITU AI for Good: Innovate for Impact (2025)
account: Researchers report energy-efficiency gains of about 9.2% from driving advice in simulations comparing battery use and travel time. The system has not been deployed. Effects on vehicle performance and emissions in practice are unknown.
purpose: Help drivers manage routes, speed, battery use, and charging.
system: AI vehicle-endurance prediction and advisory system

ratings.reason: The source supplies simulation results rather than observed driver benefits; real-world range and travel effects are unknown.
Simulated efficiency gains suggest potential for operators, but their realized operational extent is unknown.
Lower real-world emissions are intended; simulated battery use does not establish an environmental outcome.

ai_role.statement: Forecasting models and a language model generate route and driving advice in simulation. The results do not establish causal benefit in deployed vehicles.

evidence.citation: Project account in International Telecommunication Union, AI for Good: Innovate for Impact, 2025. Information current as of June 2025. Outcomes are reported by the project team. The account provides no independent outcome evaluation.
evidence.title: Use Case 9: Environment-Based Endurance Testing in Autonomous Vehicles

produced_by: Conditions that could produce the benefit are unspecified.
must_hold: Simulated or historical driving, terrain, battery, and weather data

headline: Simulating AI advice for electric-vehicle endurance
claim_basis: Sources: the makers' report. The cited evidence includes no independent source and no finding by a regulator or court.
